about: Ball flights computed by the prototype's own simulate(). Coordinates: meters, home plate at origin, center field toward NEGATIVE z (flip z for Unity), right field +x. Start point (0,0.9,0). sprayDeg 0 = dead center, negative = left field. LUCK IS PINNED: simulate() has three random moments (a 50/50 coin flip for a ball arriving within 0.4 m below the top of the wall, a 1.1% Moon hop on a bounce, and the direction and height of a kick off a bag). These cases were generated with Math.random() fixed at 0.75, so: the top-of-wall flip always takes the NOT-less-than-0.5 branch, a Moon hop never happens, and a bag kick always turns the positive way (sign +1) by 0.675 rad with an upward speed of 5.0. Run the Unity flight with the same pinned value (every random draw returns 0.75) and the same input must give the same output. A Unity port of the flight should reproduce every row within a small tolerance (suggest 0.5 m on distance and landing, 0.05 s on times, exact on the booleans). ONE ROW IS MARKED unstable:true (42 m/s, 25 up, 45 spray): a ball rolling along the corner where the line wall meets the fence, exactly on the 45-degree line, where the last digit of sin/cos differs between JavaScript engines and tips it either side of the line. Skip it. Other rows at exactly 45 degrees need the flight run in double precision to match.
